attachments.label: A1
attachments.text:
Hagenbuch Services Ltd
Uster

Ms Emma Ellis
Wiesenstrasse 14
8610 Uster

Uster, 5 June 2026

Termination of your employment

Dear Ms Ellis

We regret to inform you that we are terminating your employment with Hagenbuch Services Ltd for organisational reasons.

Please arrange a meeting with the office to discuss the handover of your current files and the return of your keys.

Yours sincerely

Rachel Bucher
Office Manager

attachments.document_title: Written probation clause (individual agreement, standard or collective contract)
attachments.label: A2
must_show: the written instrument that sets it
attachments.text:
Clause 4 - Probation period

4.1 The probation period is three months.

4.2 During the probation period the parties will hold at least one review meeting to discuss the employee's performance and integration into the team.

4.3 At the end of the probation period the employee receives a short written assessment from the line manager.

4.4 Holidays should, where possible, not be taken during the probation period.

questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Was the employee, through no fault of their own, wholly or partly prevented from working by illness or accident on the day notice was given or at some time while the notice period was running, and was the incapacity at that point still within its protected length: up to 30 days in the first year of service, 90 days in the second to fifth years, 180 days from the sixth year?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Was the employee performing Swiss compulsory military service, civil defence service or alternative civilian service on the day notice was given or while the notice period was running, or, for such a service lasting more than eleven days, did either of those fall within the four weeks before or after it?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Did the employer give the employee notice of termination of the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Was the employee pregnant, or within sixteen weeks after giving birth, on the day notice was given or while the notice period was running?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Does the file say that a written individual employment contract, a standard employment contract or a collective employment contract sets notice periods different from the statutory ones (seven days during probation, art. 335b para. 1; one month in the first year of service, two months in the second to ninth years, three months thereafter)?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Does the file say that a written individual agreement, a standard employment contract or a collective employment contract set a probation period other than the first month of employment?

questions.label: Q7
questions.question: Where a protected period (illness or accident, compulsory service, pregnancy or birth, as above) is raised: was the notice given before that period began, with the notice period not yet expired when it began?

questions.label: Q8
questions.question: Was the notice given while the probation period was still running, counting any extension of the probation period under art. 335b para. 3 (a probation period interrupted by illness, accident or a non-voluntary legal obligation is extended accordingly)?

text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I'm pregnant. My doctor confirmed it in the middle of June, and by her calculation I was already about six weeks along at the beginning of the month.

I've also attached the clause about my trial period, which you'll need further down.

A friend told me that the order of things matters, so let me be clear about it: both the pregnancy and my service had already started by the time the notice reached me. Neither of them began afterwards.

Apart from that I was perfectly fit. I wasn't ill or injured at any point, before or after the letter, and I could have worked every single day.

The service I mean is my civil defence refresher course. I'm assigned to the civil defence and I had to report for duty from 1 to 12 June 2026, as every year.

Right in the middle of that course, Hagenbuch Services Ltd gave me notice. The letter from Rachel Bucher, the office manager, is dated 5 June. I found it in my letterbox in Uster on 7 June, when I was home for the weekend. I've attached it too. My colleague Alice Wälti says Ms Bucher told the team I was leaving 'for organisational reasons'. I earn CHF 3,070 a month and I am now looking at a baby and no job.

One more detail you may need: my written contract set a trial period of three months, not the usual single month.

Can they really do this? What should I do next?

Kind regards,
Emma Ellis
Wiesenstrasse 14, Uster
